rings.label: 01 / PEOPLE
rings.text: Good work starts with people understanding each other. I help turn a room full of perspectives into a shared direction.

rings.label: 02 / PLANS
rings.text: A plan should answer three things: what happens next, who owns it, and what they need to move forward.

rings.label: 03 / COMMUNICATION
rings.text: I turn busy conversations into clear decisions, useful updates, and next steps people can act on.

rings.label: 04 / FOLLOW-THROUGH
rings.text: The small details matter: the current file, the open question, the handover that makes the next person ready.

stages.title: Start with the real question.
stages.description: Understand the intended outcome, the people involved, and the constraints. A clear brief starts with listening carefully enough to spot what has not been said.

stages.title: Make the direction shared.
stages.description: Bring the scope, deliverables, and open questions into one place. Confirm what success looks like and who needs to make each decision.

stages.title: Give the work a rhythm.
stages.description: Connect tasks to owners and references. Keep reviews focused, consolidate feedback, and make dependencies visible so the team can keep moving.

stages.title: Leave the next person ready.
stages.description: Organize final deliverables, capture outstanding responsibilities, and prepare a handover the receiving team can actually use.

decks.title: How do we get there from here?
decks.label: 01 / THE ROADMAP

slides.title:
Start with the change.
Then name the thing.
slides.note: A website is a deliverable. What does it need to help someone understand or do?

cards.label: THE QUESTION
cards.text: What should be different when we’re done?

cards.label: THE PEOPLE
cards.text: Who needs this to work?

cards.label: THE CONSTRAINT
cards.text: What do we already know is fixed?

slides.footer: First sketch: an outcome before an output.

slides.title:
A route.
Not a crystal ball.
slides.note: An illustrative sequence, with review gates instead of invented deadlines.
slides.footer: At each gate: what needs to be true before the next step?

slides.title:
What are we
waiting on?
slides.note: A visible dependency is easier to discuss than a silent delay.

cards.label: INPUT
cards.text: The latest copy, files, or access.

cards.label: DECISION
cards.text: The person who can approve the direction.

cards.label: CONSEQUENCE
cards.text: The next task that cannot start without it.

slides.footer: Working question: who can help remove the blocker?

slides.title:
If the brief moves,
move the plan deliberately.
slides.note: A new request deserves a clear conversation about what it affects.
slides.footer: A revised plan is useful when everyone is working from it.

slides.title:
Don’t just finish.
Make it usable.
slides.note: Sketch the handover from the next person’s point of view.

cards.label: FIND
cards.text: Can they locate the final files?

cards.label: UNDERSTAND
cards.text: Can they see what is still open?

cards.label: CONTINUE
cards.text: Do they know who owns the next step?

slides.footer: A good last page makes the next beginning easier.

decks.title: One big brief. A few better questions.
decks.label: 02 / HOW I THINK

slides.title:
What is the question
behind the request?
slides.note: A request tells me what someone wants made. A better conversation tells me why.

cards.label: HEAR
cards.text: What are they asking for?

cards.label: ASK
cards.text: What prompted the request?

cards.label: REFRAME
cards.text: What does success need to look like?

slides.footer: Listen long enough to understand the problem.

slides.title:
A decision is not
the same as an idea.
slides.note: Separate the conversation before turning it into tasks.

cards.label: DECIDED
cards.text: An agreed direction the team can act on.

cards.label: OPEN
cards.text: A question still waiting for the right person.

cards.label: EXPLORING
cards.text: An idea worth testing, not a commitment.

slides.footer: Useful labels keep assumptions from becoming instructions.

slides.title:
Who moves this
one step forward?
slides.note: Responsibility becomes clearer when it is attached to a specific action.
slides.footer: One clear next move is better than a vague shared intention.

slides.title:
Different people.
Different context.
slides.note: The facts stay consistent. The message meets the reader where they are.

cards.label: CLIENT
cards.text: What changed and what needs a decision?

cards.label: CONTRIBUTOR
cards.text: What should I make or revise?

cards.label: PROJECT LEAD
cards.text: What does this affect across the work?

slides.footer: The right detail is the detail that helps someone act.

slides.title:
Could someone else
pick this up?
slides.note: A simple test for a brief, a tracker, or a handover.

cards.label: CLEAR?
cards.text: Does the next step make sense?

cards.label: CURRENT?
cards.text: Are the links and decisions up to date?

cards.label: USEFUL?
cards.text: Can the person act without reconstructing the conversation?

slides.footer: Clarity is something to check, not something to assume.

slides.title:
“We need to improve
our updates.”
slides.note: Illustrative exercise: turn a broad intention into something a team can test.

cards.label: TOO BROAD
cards.text: Improve communication.

cards.label: A BETTER QUESTION
cards.text: Where do people lose the context they need?

cards.label: FIRST HYPOTHESIS
cards.text: The next action is buried in the update.

slides.footer: A working hypothesis is a place to begin, not a proven conclusion.

slides.title:
What if every update
had a clearer ending?
slides.note: A sketch of an update format to try in an appropriate project.
slides.footer: Prototype the habit before making a bigger system.

slides.title:
Does this help the
person receiving it?
slides.note: The person using the update can reveal what the draft is missing.

cards.label: ASK
cards.text: What did you need to look for?

cards.label: NOTICE
cards.text: Which parts still needed clarification?

cards.label: CHECK
cards.text: Was the next action understood?

slides.footer: Feedback on the process is part of improving the process.

slides.title:
Keep the useful bit.
Rewrite the rest.
slides.note: A draft should be allowed to change when the evidence changes.

cards.label: KEEP
cards.text: The part that made the next action clearer.

cards.label: REMOVE
cards.text: Repeated context that obscured the request.

cards.label: REWORK
cards.text: The question that still produced confusion.

slides.footer: Iteration means responding to what you learn.

slides.title:
What would make
the next version better?
slides.note: An honest work-in-progress page ends with a useful question.

cards.label: UNKNOWN
cards.text: Will the format work for a different audience?

cards.label: NEXT TEST
cards.text: Adapt the level of detail, keep the same facts.

cards.label: REMINDER
cards.text: This is an illustrative exercise, not a reported project result.

slides.footer: Not finished. Clear enough to keep moving.

slides.title:
A blank page.
Some useful questions.
slides.note: Prepare enough context to listen well, without assuming the answer.

cards.label: LOOK UP
cards.text: What has already been shared: the request, references, current assets.

cards.label: WRITE DOWN
cards.text: What is unclear: purpose, audience, timing, ownership.

cards.label: BRING
cards.text: A simple agenda: context → goal → constraints → next steps.

slides.footer: Margin note: don’t let the agenda stop a useful question.

slides.title:
Listen for the
problem underneath.
slides.note: Capture what the client means, not only the deliverable they name.

cards.label: GOAL
cards.text: What should the work help someone understand, feel, or do?

cards.label: PEOPLE
cards.text: Who is the audience? Who contributes? Who decides?

cards.label: CONSTRAINTS
cards.text: What is fixed? What is flexible? Which inputs are missing?

slides.footer: Circle the assumptions. Do not turn them into facts.

slides.title:
Three piles.
Less confusion.
slides.note: Sort the conversation while the context is still fresh.

cards.label: AGREED
cards.text: Confirmed decisions, scope boundaries, and responsibilities.

cards.label: OPEN
cards.text: Questions awaiting a specific person or missing input.

cards.label: POSSIBLE
cards.text: Ideas to explore; not yet promised deliverables.

slides.footer: Scratch out “we all agreed” unless you can name the decision.

slides.title:
Send the version
everyone can act on.
slides.note: A call summary should bridge the conversation and the next action.

cards.label: RECAP
cards.text: The intended outcome and the decisions made.

cards.label: NEXT
cards.text: Actions by person, supporting links, and agreed review dates.

cards.label: CONFIRM
cards.text: Ask the relevant people to correct misunderstandings or fill gaps.

slides.footer: Attach the reference or recording only where appropriate.

slides.title: Check the starting line.
slides.note: The call is complete. The project definition may still need work.

cards.label: ENOUGH TO START
cards.text: A goal, a point of contact, and a clear scoping task.

cards.label: STILL MISSING
cards.text: An asset inventory? Copy? Access? Name the source and owner.

cards.label: NEXT PAGE
cards.text: Move into the brief with open questions visibly tracked.

slides.footer: Output: an agreed summary, not a promise made from incomplete information.

slides.title:
What is this
work for?
slides.note: Start the brief with the outcome and the audience.

cards.label: PURPOSE
cards.text: Explain the problem the project should address.

cards.label: AUDIENCE
cards.text: Name who will use the work and what they need from it.

cards.label: SUCCESS
cards.text: Agree observable acceptance criteria; don’t invent performance claims.

slides.footer: A deliverable list is necessary. It is not the whole brief.

slides.title:
In. Out.
Still to decide.
slides.note: Make the scope easy to discuss before production begins.

cards.label: IN SCOPE
cards.text: List deliverables, formats, versions, and agreed review rounds.

cards.label: OUT OF SCOPE
cards.text: Record the relevant exclusions so assumptions don’t grow unnoticed.

cards.label: OPEN
cards.text: Name what still needs a decision and who can make it.

slides.footer: Rough edge: “etc.” is not a helpful deliverable.

slides.title:
What must arrive
before we can make it?
slides.note: Connect each input to the work it enables.

cards.label: CONTENT
cards.text: Copy, descriptions, imagery, and source material.

cards.label: ACCESS
cards.text: Relevant platforms, file permissions, and approved assets.

cards.label: DECISIONS
cards.text: Brand direction, format choices, and the final approver.

slides.footer: No invented dates: agree the input timing with the owner.

slides.title:
Who reviews what?
And when?
slides.note: Avoid sending every question to every person.

cards.label: DIRECTION
cards.text: Who confirms the concept or approach?

cards.label: DETAIL
cards.text: Who checks copy, accuracy, and practical use?

cards.label: FINAL
cards.text: Who has authority to accept the deliverable?

slides.footer: One person collecting comments may not be the final approver.

slides.title:
A brief can change.
The agreement must stay clear.
slides.note: Keep the current brief connected to the project tracker.

cards.label: CONFIRM
cards.text: Share the brief for the relevant approvals.

cards.label: LINK
cards.text: Attach it to the project with the working references.

cards.label: CHANGE
cards.text: Record scope updates and their delivery implications.

slides.footer: Output: a usable brief, clear owners, and a visible list of open inputs.

decks.title: Review, revise, and find the current version.
decks.label: 06 / THE FEEDBACK LOOP

slides.title:
Make the review
question specific.
slides.note: The type of review determines the feedback you need.

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.text: What is this version intended to demonstrate?

cards.label: QUESTION
cards.text: Are we reviewing direction, content, execution, or final quality?

cards.label: LINK
cards.text: Share one current version, with the appropriate viewing access.

slides.footer: Write the question before you write “thoughts?”

slides.title:
Many comments.
One working list.
slides.note: Collect the feedback without erasing the context.

cards.label: CAPTURE
cards.text: The comment, the relevant section, and its source.

cards.label: GROUP
cards.text: Required changes, clarification requests, and optional explorations.

cards.label: LINK
cards.text: Connect each point to the version being reviewed.

slides.footer: Illustrative log: page / comment / decision / owner / status.

slides.title:
These two notes
pull in different directions.
slides.note: Resolve the conflict before asking the team to execute.

cards.label: SPOT
cards.text: Which comments cannot both be followed?

cards.label: ASK
cards.text: What outcome matters most, and who can decide?

cards.label: RECORD
cards.text: Write the agreed direction where the team will find it.

slides.footer: Do not make the contributor guess which stakeholder to follow.

slides.title:
A change list
someone can work from.
slides.note: Turn approved direction into specific tasks.

cards.label: ASSIGN
cards.text: Give each revision an owner and the supporting reference.

cards.label: CHECK
cards.text: Review dependent pages, formats, and deliverables affected.

cards.label: UPDATE
cards.text: Track changes addressed and questions still open.

slides.footer: Link each task to the right file rather than a folder of old versions.

slides.title:
Review again.
Or move forward.
slides.note: Ask for the right decision at the end of the round.

cards.label: SUMMARIZE
cards.text: What changed since the previous version?

cards.label: CONFIRM
cards.text: What is now approved and what still needs a decision?

cards.label: PROCEED
cards.text: Record approval before moving to dependent work.

slides.footer: If scope changed, return to the brief—not just another revision round.

decks.title: The handoff: leave the next person ready.
decks.label: 07 / THE RECEIVING END

slides.title:
Start with
the receiving team.
slides.note: The handover should fit what the next person needs to do.

cards.label: CLIENT
cards.text: Needs to find final assets and understand how to use them.

cards.label: DEVELOPER
cards.text: Needs the relevant files, decisions, and implementation context.

cards.label: PROJECT OWNER
cards.text: Needs to see responsibilities, open items, and next steps.

slides.footer: One package can serve several people if its structure is clear.

slides.title:
What did we
agree to deliver?
slides.note: Check the final package against the latest approved scope.

cards.label: MATCH
cards.text: List each agreed deliverable and its final location.

cards.label: VERIFY
cards.text: Check exports, file names, formats, and versions.

cards.label: SEPARATE
cards.text: Keep superseded drafts out of the final delivery path.

slides.footer: Cross-check approved scope changes as well as the first brief.

slides.title:
Click the links.
Actually open the files.
slides.note: A finished folder is not enough if the recipient cannot use it.

cards.label: ACCESS
cards.text: Confirm intended recipients have the appropriate permissions.

cards.label: CONTENT
cards.text: Check completeness, naming, and relevant quality criteria.

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.text: Explain essential usage details, dependencies, and limitations.

slides.footer: A broken link can undo an otherwise thoughtful handover.

slides.title:
Keep the loose ends
in plain sight.
slides.note: Separate unfinished responsibilities from completed delivery.

cards.label: ITEM
cards.text: What remains open and why?

cards.label: OWNER
cards.text: Who is responsible for moving it forward?

cards.label: NEXT STEP
cards.text: What action or decision is needed, and when will it be checked?

slides.footer: A clean document should not hide an unresolved dependency.

slides.title:
Could you use this
without the meetings?
slides.note: Read the handover as someone joining for the first time.

cards.label: FIND
cards.text: Can you locate the approved final files quickly?

cards.label: UNDERSTAND
cards.text: Can you tell what the package contains and what remains open?

cards.label: CONTINUE
cards.text: Do you know the next action and the appropriate contact?

slides.footer: Output: final files + a usable map + visible responsibilities.

decks.title: Close the project. Keep the lesson.
decks.label: 08 / THE CLOSEOUT

slides.title:
Done needs
a shared meaning.
slides.note: Use the agreed acceptance criteria to close the work.

cards.label: DELIVERED
cards.text: The latest agreed deliverables are accounted for.

cards.label: ACCEPTED
cards.text: Required reviews and decisions are recorded.

cards.label: TRANSFERRED
cards.text: The next owner has the information and access needed.

slides.footer: An internal task status is not always the same as client acceptance.

slides.title:
Archive the useful
story of the work.
slides.note: Keep the context someone might reasonably need later.

cards.label: FILES
cards.text: Approved final deliverables and their source locations.

cards.label: DECISIONS
cards.text: Important choices and the context behind them.

cards.label: RESPONSIBILITIES
cards.text: Relevant remaining follow-ups and ownership.

slides.footer: Follow the project’s access and retention requirements.

slides.title:
Where did the
work get difficult?
slides.note: A retrospective should make the next project easier.

cards.label: KEEP
cards.text: Which habit or tool helped the team deliver?

cards.label: CHANGE
cards.text: Where did ambiguity or repeated friction slow things down?

cards.label: UNDERSTAND
cards.text: What conditions caused the problem, beyond one person’s action?

slides.footer: Be specific enough that a process can change.

slides.title:
A lesson needs
a next action too.
slides.note: Choose a bounded improvement instead of a long list of intentions.

cards.label: EXAMPLE
cards.text: Add a reviewer field to the task template.

cards.label: OWNER
cards.text: Name who will update the template.

cards.label: CHECK
cards.text: Review whether it helped on the next appropriate project.

slides.footer: Illustrative improvement—not a claim about a past result.

slides.title:
Carry the learning.
Leave the clutter.
slides.note: Give the next project a clearer starting point.

cards.label: REUSE
cards.text: The useful brief, review, and handover patterns.

cards.label: ADAPT
cards.text: Change the process to fit the next team and goal.

cards.label: REPEAT
cards.text: Listen, align, move, close—and keep asking better questions.

slides.footer: The final sketch becomes the beginning of the next useful version.
